thread.title_full: Glen Hansard's funeral in Dublin attended by Bono and Eddie Vedder

author: Sofia Alvarez Entertainment Editor
title: Glen Hansard's funeral in Dublin attended by Bono and Eddie Vedder
text:
Hundreds of mourners, including global music icons Bono and Eddie Vedder, gathered at St Patrick’s Cathedral in Dublin on August 4, 2026, for the funeral of Academy Award-winning singer-songwriter Glen Hansard. The 56-year-old musician died in a single-vehicle motorcycle crash on the outskirts of Dublin on July 29.
The service was a massive communal event, with fans queuing for hours outside the cathedral and thousands more watching via live-stream. Inside, the atmosphere was defined by the music Hansard spent over three decades creating, while outside, large screens allowed those unable to fit inside the cathedral to witness the farewell to a man described by peers as a cultural icon .
A Musical Send-off at St Patrick’s Cathedral The funeral service was structured as a musical tribute, weaving together performances from Hansard’s most significant collaborators. Pearl Jam’s Eddie Vedder performed Hansard’s The Song of Good Hope alongside Markéta Irglová, Hansard’s long-time musical partner. The performance also included members of The Frames, the rock band Hansard led for many years.
Photo: asiaone.com U2’s Bono played a central role in the tributes, reciting lyrics from the track “Beautiful Day” and encouraging the congregation to join in. In a personal touch, Bono played a voicemail message from Patti Smith , who performed a lullaby for Hansard’s family and friends.
As the wicker coffin, topped with flowers, was carried out of the cathedral, the crowd engaged in a mass singalong of Bob Dylan’s “Forever Young.” The procession eventually led to a private ceremony at Mount Jerome.
Family Tributes and the Loss of a Father Hansard’s widow, Finnish poet Maire Saaritsa, led the family tributes. She read a poem written early in their relationship and thanked her husband for the life we shared, searching for truth and beauty side by side . Saaritsa also expressed gratitude to the police officers who responded to the crash site.
Glen Hansard’s wife Maire Saaritsa speaks at funeral service of the late musician Glen Hansard, Oscar-Winning ‘Once’ Star, Dies in Dublin Motorcycle Crash at 56
The couple’s 3-year-old son, Christy, did not attend the service. Saaritsa explained that he was too young to witness or understand an event of such scale , though she noted that the bright spirit he inherited from his father is with us .
“Glen’s remarkable gifts and outstanding talent, which touched so many hearts, took him from the streets of Dublin to audiences across the globe.”
William Morton, Dean of St Patrick’s Cathedral
The Fatal Crash in Lucan The tragedy occurred in the early hours of Wednesday, July 29, on the outskirts of Dublin. According to Irish police, a man in his 50s died in a single-vehicle motorcycle crash in Lucan before 4:30 a.m. local time. Other reports specify the collision happened in the Strawberry Beds on the R109 Lower Road, between Rugged Lane and Tinkers Hill.
Photo: 1News The timing of the accident was particularly poignant; Hansard had been participating in a traditional music session at The Wren’s Nest pub just hours before the crash. He had also recently completed a homecoming performance at Dublin’s Trinity Summer Series and was in the midst of promoting his “Don’t Settle” releases and an Irish tour.
Glen Hansard, Oscar-winning songwriter, dies in Dublin motorcycle crash
A Legacy of Activism and Artistry Hansard’s career was defined by a transition from Dublin street busker to international award-winner. He first gained wider attention in the 1991 film The Commitments , playing the guitarist Outspan Foster. His most significant commercial success came with the 2007 film Once , for which he and Markéta Irglová won an Academy Award in 2008 for the song Falling Slowly. The film was later adapted for Broadway, winning eight Tony Awards in 2012.
Photo: 1news Beyond the stage and screen, Hansard was deeply embedded in social causes. He was the driving force behind the annual Christmas Eve busk outside Dublin’s Gaiety Theatre, a tradition he started 16 years ago to raise funds for the Simon Community homelessness charity. His activism extended to the housing crisis in Ireland and support for Ukraine, including recording the song “Take Heart” with Ukrainian refugees.
“Sometimes I would wonder if Glen Hansard really existed… seriously, he was such an angelic presence… not otherworldly… in fact, very present this presence. A smiling rascal if you needed him to be… this most musical and mischievous archangel of Ballymun… no airs, plenty of graces.”

Bono
The ‘Celebration of Life’ Afters at Vicar Street The formal mourning transitioned into a high-energy tribute shortly after the burial. Family and friends gathered at Vicar Street for an event billed as Glen Hansard’s Celebration of Life. This private “afters gig saw Eddie Vedder lead a cover of Neil Young’s Rockin’ in the Free World, backed by The Frames and Imelda May.
Funeral of Glen Hansard in Dublin | RTÉ News The event also featured tributes from Hansard’s nieces, Amy and Sinead, who performed on the Vicar Street stage. The gathering was attended by “The Framily”—dedicated fans of The Frames who traveled from as far as Germany and the United States to honor the musician.
The scale of the response—from a public wake at the Irish Museum of Modern Art that drew over 11,000 people to the presence of figures like Steve Coogan, Chris O’Dowd, and former Sinn Féin president Gerry Adams—underscores Hansard’s role not just as a musician, but as a connective tissue in the Irish cultural landscape.

As the wicker coffin, topped with flowers, was carried out of the cathedral, the crowd engaged in a mass singalong of Bob Dylan’s “Forever Young.” The procession eventually led to a private ceremony at Mount Jerome. He had also recently completed a homecoming performance at Dublin’s Trinity Summer Series and was in the midst of promoting his “Don’t Settle” releases and an Irish tour.
